metadata.title: Simple critical zeros in short intervals: stability, pressure, and parity
metadata.description:
Let c(θ) = 2 - θ/2 - cot(θ/√2)/√2, and let θ_0 be its unique zero in (0,1). We combine the finite stable rank-trace inequality underlying recent zeta-zero results with a classical positive density of distinct odd-multiplicity critical zeros. If κ > 0 is one fixed Selberg density constant packed into every longer interval, then, for each fixed 0.51 < θ < 1, the lower asymptotic simple-critical proportion in (T, T + T^θ] is at least max{0, c(θ), (c(θ) + 2κ)/3}. Consequently it is positive at some fixed exponent strictly below θ_0. A separate multiplicity identity gives the correct distinct-zero companion, including a proportion greater than one half at another exponent below θ_0. The new exponents are expressed in terms of the unevaluated classical constant; no new decimal exponent is claimed.

We also strengthen the entire positive cosine curve by an odd-frame pressure transfer. A two-variable interval certificate at θ = 3/4 yields the simple-critical bound 0.4190878881701117... and distinct bound 0.7095439440850558....

The finite stability inequality, the classical sign-change theorems, and the global pressure methods are prior work. Wang's fixed-test pair-correlation theorem supplies the arithmetic input; all smoothing and support limits follow the height limit. The qualitative parity result requires no numerical zero sampling or kernel optimization. No global record, effective starting height, or solution of the Riemann hypothesis is claimed.

Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (problems/number-theory/riemann-hypothesis).
